page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, 8.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per core, and no local storage. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves average results in single-core metrics, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1842.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1556.0. However, multi-core and memory subsystem performance are constrained. The stress-ng multi-core score of 1932.39 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1815.0 fall into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large block read-only speeds at 15.1 GB/sec and write speeds at 13.63 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%.

Given the performance profile, this instance is suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads such as basic text processing or simple web serving. It exhibits weak performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, making it less suitable for high-throughput database hosting. The lack of local storage and low baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps further restrict its use to non-I/O-intensive tasks. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES cryptography, which assist in basic encryption tasks, but the overall resource density and low multi-core scaling limit its utility for complex parallel computing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.large is a general-purpose, x86_64 architecture server instance utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.9 GHz, 8.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage. The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1556.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1842.18. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the bottom 10% tier, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1815.0 and a large-block memory read speed of 15.1 GB/sec. This server is suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving, but it is constrained for database operations or parallel computing workloads due to its limited multi-core scaling and memory throughput.
